LESSON: READING 1.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What is the importance of fluency in reading?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a text with accuracy and fluency for information
2. respond to direct and inferential questions from a text for comprehension

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 1.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 1.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read a text with accuracy and fluency for information

What this means
In this part you learn to read a text with accuracy and fluency for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read a text with accuracy and fluency for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read a text with accuracy and fluency for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Respond to direct and inferential questions from a text for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to direct and inferential questions from a text for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to direct and inferential questions from a text for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to direct and inferential questions from a text for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read a text with accuracy and fluency for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information to a partner. (skill: respond to direct and inferential questions from a text for comprehension)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read a text with accuracy and fluency for information.
3. Practise this skill: respond to direct and inferential questions from a text for comprehension.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is the importance of fluency in reading?
2. Why should we preserve cultural attire in our community?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read a text with accuracy and fluency for information.
5. Be able to: respond to direct and inferential questions from a text for comprehension.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
